result.instructions: Lambo agentic graph memory for session 'kalari-b4'. Call lambo_recall before acting on a task to load relevant prior memory, lambo_derive and lambo_record_action to write what you learned and did, lambo_reserve before editing a shared concept, and lambo_inspect / lambo_saints / lambo_stats to look around. A concept is one fact, stated atomically and short, such as a decision with its reason; it is not a log line or a paragraph, and activity goes to lambo_record_action. When a write rests on a ruling or decision recall showed you, cite it by its id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) in depends_on: lambo_record_action's, or the concept's on lambo_derive. When a write shows an existing concept to be wrong, name it the same way in against. Every tool takes your agent_id: use one stable id for as long as you run, never one per call, task or topic: your model or client id (<your-model-id>), with a stable instance suffix if several of you run at once. It is caller-asserted and unverified. Work is recorded under it, so a stable id keeps attribution whole. Soft locks are held under it: distinct ids contend for a node, and callers sharing an id share its locks and can release each other's, so concurrent agents that must keep out of each other's edits need distinct stable ids. created_at is server-stamped: do not send a client flush timestamp. lambo_derive and lambo_record_action may take optional RFC3339 event_time for historical about-time, such as a commit or document date; omit it for a live fact, which is about now. Ordering is yours to manage, and writes are applied in the BACKGROUND: lambo_derive and lambo_record_action return once your input is validated and ordered, and their ack carries a receipt id. Their outcome arrives on your next tool response. If you need a write visible to the very next read, call lambo_stats with that receipt and a wait_ms first; otherwise carry on — writes you send one after another are applied in that order (two you fire at once have no order to keep).

tools.name: lambo_derive
tools.description: Derive concepts from the current interaction into session memory. A concept is one fact, stated atomically and short enough that a later restatement of the same fact matches it, such as a decision with its reason. Good: 'Lease TTL is 45s because it must exceed the 15s shutdown budget'. Bad: a paragraph narrating what you did and found. It is not a log: record activity with lambo_record_action. To group facts under a decision, send each as its own concept and add parent_of pairs with the decision as parent and each fact as child. When a concept rests on a ruling or decision already in memory, cite it by id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) in that concept's depends_on: it must already exist and match exactly one concept, or the whole call is refused. When a concept says an existing one is wrong, name that one the same way in the concept's against: it records the contradiction, dated by this write's event_time (else now), and adds no dependent, score or promotion. A settled outcome may list replacement_candidates: existing concepts of the same type, very close to a new one, that it may replace. Nothing is recorded for them; cite one in against on a later call only if the new concept really replaces it. A candidate marked newer is dated after the new concept: it may replace the new one, so never cite it in against. created_at is stamped server-side. event_time is optional RFC3339 historical about-time, such as a commit or document date; omit it for a live fact, which is about now. Returns as soon as the input is validated and ordered — the write is applied in the background and the ack carries a receipt id. The outcome is piggybacked on your next tool response; to wait for it, call lambo_stats with that receipt and a wait_ms. On a store with vector search each concept is embedded with the whole call's text, so a concept sent alone may be at most 8189 bytes; a longer call is refused before the ack, naming the part that is too long. scope (optional) writes to one of this session's shared layers instead; writes to different sessions have no ordering between them.

against.description:
Optional: up to 8 existing concepts this one contradicts, such as an
older belief a newer observation shows is wrong. Name each as for
`depends_on`: its id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) or full
node id (its exact content also works). Each must already exist in
the session the write goes to and match exactly one concept other
than this one, or the whole call is refused before the ack and
nothing is written, as is a concept this one also lists in
`depends_on`. Recorded as this concept contradicting each, dated by
this write's `event_time` (else when it is written) whatever the two
concepts' ages; sending it again does not re-date it. It adds no
dependent and changes no score or promotion, and raises no conflict;
it does count as a fresh write to the contradicted concept. Recall
then warns on the contradicted concept and shows this one beside it.
Naming the other concept of a pair recall marks possibly superseded
settles it: the mark is removed. At most 32 across the call.

content.description:
The concept text: one fact, stated atomically and short — a sentence,
not a paragraph or a log of what you did.

depends_on.description:
Optional: up to 8 existing concepts this one rests on, such as the
ruling a decision applies. Cite each by its id: the 8 hex characters
recall shows, or its full node id (its exact content also works).
Each must already exist in this session and match exactly one
concept; one that does not, or that names this concept itself,
refuses the whole call before the ack and writes nothing. Recorded as
this concept depending on each, which makes the cited concept
load-bearing. Citing the other concept of a pair recall marks
possibly superseded settles it: the mark is removed. At most 32
across the call.

WireConceptType.description:
What kind of thing a concept is. Pick the one that fits the content best:

- `entity` — a named thing: a person, service, file, table, or component.
- `logic` — a rule, decision, or piece of reasoning about how things work.
- `constraint` — a requirement or limit that must keep holding.
- `resource` — something produced, consumed, or acted on by the work.
- `observation` — something noticed in passing; the weakest kind, and
  the only one that can later be demoted.

WireReference.description:
One `depends_on` or `against` entry: an existing concept, by the id
recall shows, its full node id or its exact content.

agent_id.description:
Id of the agent making this call. Use one stable id for the agent's
whole life, never one per call, task or topic (good: your model or
client id, such as `claude-opus-5-5` or `gpt-5.6`, with a stable
instance suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad:
`b1-review`, `implement-m12`). Caller-asserted and unverified: work is
recorded under exactly the id you send, so a stable id keeps your
attribution whole. Agents sharing an id share soft locks and can
release each other's; concurrent agents that must keep out of each
other's edits need distinct stable ids.

concepts.description: Concepts to derive from this interaction.

event_time.description:
Optional RFC3339 historical about-time for this evidence, such as a
commit or document date. Omit it for a live fact, which is about now.
No additional date-range bounds are applied.

parent_of.description:
Optional `(parent, child)` hierarchy pairs. Both ends resolve (and may
be created) as concepts.

repo_scope.description:
Optional: the repository this call's path-like `resource` concepts
and `parent_of` ends belong to, so that `README.md` in two
repositories is two concepts. Not the session written to (that is
`scope`). Send one stable id per repository, the same from every clone
and worktree: its remote as `host/owner/repo` (no scheme, credentials,
query or `.git`), or for a local-only repository an agreed unique root
name: at most 512 bytes, with no whitespace or invisible characters
inside. Taken as given, never verified; compared exactly after
trimming.
A path is matched as exact text (case and `./` count), never resolved
on disk. With it, path text names only this repository's concept and
never falls back to an unscoped one; cite an older concept by its id.
In a shared layer it lets a relative path through on the entries it
covers. Omit it to keep the unscoped identity.

tools.name: lambo_reserve
tools.description: Take a soft lock on a memory node before editing it (or release one). Reservations are advisory and do not survive a server restart. The lock is held under the agent_id you send, which is caller-asserted and unverified: a distinct id gets a distinct lock, and callers sharing an id share the lock. scope (optional) names one of this session's shared layers, for a node from that layer.

suffix such as `-worker-2` if several run at once; bad: `b1-review`).
Caller-asserted and unverified: locks are cooperative. Distinct ids
contend: reserving a node another id holds is refused, naming the

Answers what happened to that one write: applied, failed, dropped,
pending, expired, restart-lost or never-issued. Receipts are scoped to

wait_ms.description:
With `receipt`, wait up to this many milliseconds for the write to be
applied before answering — the opt-in synchrony that restores
read-your-writes when you need it. Clamped to the server's own maximum.
Ignored without `receipt`.

The published maximum is [`crate::writeq::RECEIPT_WAIT_MAX`] in
milliseconds — a client that sends more is clamped to it rather than
refused, and `the_published_wait_maximum_is_the_real_one` pins the
literal below to the constant (T88-H4 requires a *published* maximum,
and `schemars` takes a literal).
